title: Avin (Ravin) bar (Rav) Chisda
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In Gittin 5b, Ravin bar Rav Chisda brought a bill of divorce before R’ Yohanan; Hyman also cites Jerusalem Talmud Gittin, chapter 1, halakhah 1 [supplied continuation: -ב]. Bereshit Rabbah 11:2 has Avin bar Chisdai saying that it must be lowered. Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:3 has Avun bar Chisdi saying, “There are places where they call zaharah saharah.” Tanchuma, Ki Tisa 1, attributes this saying to Avin bar Rav Chisda; Hyman’s printed Pesikta Rabbati citation, Ki Tisa, ס״ב, gives Avin bar Chisda. Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:9 has Avun bar Chisdi saying, “In some places they call albanya sansanya.” In Shabbat 147b, according to the Rif, Rosh and Dikdukei Soferim readings reported by Hyman, Avun bar Rav Chisda said in the name of R’ Yohanan, “It must be tied,” etc. Hyman explains that this is what Yuchasin means by Avin bar Chisda reporting R’ Yohanan at the end of chapter Chavit.

notes.text: The supplied Pesikta Avtei label remains uncertain. Zaharah/saharah and albanya/sansanya are kept as the reported lexical forms without supplying an unsupported “sun” or botanical identification.

No new whole primary scalar was returned for this notice. Rif, Rosh and Tanchuma Buber hits remain snippets, not whole witnesses, and do not identify פסקתא אבתי. The heading preserves the optional Rav before the father; it is not transferred to bare Chisda/Chisdai/Chisdi occurrences. Every Yochanan title in the supplied passage is abbreviated and remains R-prime. The supplied Jerusalem Talmud locator is chapter 1 halakhah 1 followed by -ב; it does not establish 2a. The Pesikta locator ס״ב remains literal because neither section 2 nor 62 has been established. Earlier expanded locators and lexical interpretations are retained in historical versions rather than silently adopted. Zaharah/saharah and albanya/sansanya remain reported lexical forms, without sun, moon or botanical identification. The final Yuchasin comparison belongs to Hyman, not an identity merger. All source holds remain.

Hyman’s printed volume I, p. 95, reads Pesikta Rabbati where the supplied text has אבתי. The consulted Pesikta Rabbati 10, Ki Tisa, has (אביו) [אבין] בן חסדא and expressly gives sihara as a name for the moon. The consulted Tanchuma Buber likewise explicitly says moon, while Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:3 has Avun bar Chisdai. The Vilna digital Rif (Shabbat 62b) and Rosh (chapter 22) read Avin bar Rav Chisda. The consulted Bavli Shabbat 147b leaves the tying rule unnamed and gives the shoulder specification in the name of Rabbi Yohanan through Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba. The exact edition behind Hyman’s locator ס״ב and his reported Dikdukei Soferim and Yuchasin readings remain unverified.
